narrative.overview: Preserve the incumbent Gitmatrix identity: warm charcoal panes, Figtree text, Geist Mono identifiers and restrained amber actions. The product is a working environment for humans and agents, not a marketing dashboard. Hierarchy comes from readable content, tonal surfaces and explicit state.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal depth with amber selection and primary actions.
Persistent context and visible recovery from uncertainty.

rules.name: The State Meaning Rule
rules.body: Amber means action or selection, green means ready/evidence, violet means claim/checkpoint, and danger tokens mean blocked work or a conflict requiring attention.

dos: Do reuse semantic runtime tokens and existing component states.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, readable labels and explicit disabled-action explanations.
Do keep long-form context readable and mobile controls reachable.
Do distinguish navigation, inert metadata and mutation actions.
donts: Don't rebrand this extension or substitute a new visual world.
Don't use color alone to communicate ownership, readiness or conflict.
Don't hide uncertain writes or discard a draft to make the interface look successful.
Don't invent product claims, decorative charts or production demonstration records.
